Work in /opt/nxeon (Proxmox host running a VPS hosting platform). You are fixing BACKUPS — currently the platform's own data exists in exactly one place on one machine. Read `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` for context (do not edit it).

VERIFIED FACTS (I just checked the live box — trust these):
- DB backups WORK: `scripts/backup-db.sh` → `/tank/backup/db`, daily 03:15, 10 files present, retention 14 days.
- **Whole-VM backups have NEVER RUN.** `systemctl show nxeon-backup-vms.service -p ExecMainStartTimestamp` is EMPTY. Timer is `Sun 04:31` weekly. Find out why it has never fired and fix it.
- The only archives in `/tank/backup/dump` are a CUSTOMER's own backups of vmid 102 (12:07, 12:22 today) — not platform backups.
- Off-site (`scripts/backup-offsite.sh`) runs daily and exits 0 with "NOT CONFIGURED"; `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` has every target commented out.
- Proxmox storage `backup` = 3.7 TB, 0.06% used. `/tank/backup/db` and `/tank/backup/dump` are the real paths.

YOU OWN EXACTLY: `lib/proxmox.ts`, `worker/index.ts`, `worker/backup-schedule.ts`, `scripts/backup-*.sh`, `scripts/verify-restore.sh` (if present), systemd unit/timer/drop-in files for `nxeon-backup-*`, and a NEW admin page `app/admin/backups/page.tsx` plus any component it needs under `components/admin/` (create new files; do not modify existing admin components other than adding your nav entry — see below). Nothing else; 7 other agents are working concurrently. `prisma/schema.prisma` is FROZEN.

FIX:

**1. DATA-LOSS BUG (highest priority).** `lib/proxmox.ts:413-429` `pruneBackups` filters only on `vmid` across the whole shared `backup` storage. A CUSTOMER's manual backup therefore prunes and DELETES the platform's own host-level VM backups written by `scripts/backup-vms.sh` for that same vmid. Scope customer pruning so it can only ever delete backups the customer's own flow created (e.g. distinguish by vzdump notes/`notes-template`, a filename marker, or by restricting to a customer-specific storage/prefix) — and never touch platform archives. This must be provably safe, not best-effort.

**2. Customer backup prune only runs after a SUCCESSFUL backup** (`worker/index.ts:751-758`), so a failing or disabled schedule leaves archives forever. Add a standalone retention sweep. `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP = 2` is the agreed limit.

**3. Make whole-system backups actually happen, at the cadence the owner asked for:** "back up the entire system once every day, store the latest 3." Today the VM timer is weekly keeping 2 (drop-in `NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP=2`) and DB retention is 14 days. Make VM backups DAILY keeping 3. Also back up `/etc/pve` (Proxmox cluster config — currently nothing does, and without it a bare-metal rebuild loses every VM definition).

**4. Off-site.** Make `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` fail LOUDLY and visibly when unconfigured rather than exiting 0 pretending success — an inert backup that reports OK is worse than none. Document exactly what the owner must set (`OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` or `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`) and surface the unconfigured state in the admin UI from item 5.

**5. NEW ADMIN PAGE — `/admin/backups`.** The owner just asked "where are the backups for the entire server?" and the answer was "there is no such page". Build it: list DB dumps (path, size, age) and VM archives (vmid + hostname, size, age) read from disk / `pvesm`; show each timer's last-run and next-run and flag any that have NEVER run (that would have caught this); show off-site status prominently (configured vs not, last successful sync); show restore-verification status. Add ONE nav entry for it in `app/admin/layout.tsx` — that single file edit is permitted, keep it minimal and match the existing nav shape. Match the Nxeon dark theme exactly: reuse `.card`, `PageHeader`, `Badge`, `StatusDot`, existing slate/brand/navy classes. Invent no new visual styles. Gate with the same `requireArea(...)` pattern other admin pages use.

REQUIREMENTS
- Read-only where you can; this is a live production host with real customer VMs. NEVER delete a backup as part of testing. You may RUN read-only commands (`pvesm status`, `ls`, `systemctl show`, `vzdump --help`) but do NOT run `vzdump` for real and do NOT start/restart services.
- Comment style: explain WHY, cite the real failure prevented.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT run `npm run build`/`npm run dev`, do NOT restart or start any systemd service (you may EDIT unit files; I will reload).
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`.
- Do NOT git commit/push. Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma. Do NOT write to the live database.

Report: root cause of why VM backups never ran, exactly how you made customer pruning safe, the new cadences, and what the owner must still set for off-site.

3	Audit of the engineering session transcript `4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc.jsonl`

7	live codebase at `/opt/nxeon`** (HEAD `8e93b13`, `origin/main` in sync).
8	
9	The standard applied throughout: *code existing is not the same as the feature working.* A server
10	action nobody calls, a status computed and then overwritten by its caller, a flag that silently
11	switches a real integration into simulation — all count as **NOT DONE**, regardless of how complete
12	the implementation looks.

16	## Executive summary
17	
18	### Counts
19	
20	| | User instructions | Assistant recommendations | Total |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| **DONE** | 40 | 17 | **57** |
23	| **PARTIAL** | 14 | 8 | **22** |
24	| **NOT DONE** | 6 | 18 | **24** |
25	| **UNCLEAR / external** | 1 | 3 | **4** |

29	Headline: the *feature* work of the last 24 hours largely landed. What did not land is the
30	**trust layer** — the places where the platform tells a paying customer something that is not true.
31	Nine of the top ten gaps below are of that kind, and three of them move real money.
32	
33	### CRITICAL — found during this audit, ranks above everything below
34	
35	**Any customer can take over another customer's email domain, reset the password on their live
36	mailboxes, and then read and send mail as them.** This was surfaced by a QA agent still running from
37	the original session (`docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`) and I verified the whole chain independently:
38	
39	1. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-256` — the "one subscription per domain" check is scoped to the
40	   **caller**: `where: { userId: user.id, domainName: name, … }`. It never asks whether another user
41	   already holds that domain.
42	2. `prisma/schema.prisma:604` — `EmailSubscription.domainName` is a plain `String` with **no
43	   `@unique`**, so the database does not stop it either. `Mailbox.address` (`:623`) is likewise not
44	   unique.
45	3. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:491-538` `addMailbox` checks only `sub.userId !== user.id`, and its
46	   duplicate check (`:514`) is scoped to *that subscription's own* mailboxes. The attacker can
47	   therefore create `admin@victim.com` under their own subscription. No DNS-verification gate applies.
48	4. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:684-707` `resetMailboxPassword` validates
49	   `mailbox.subscription.userId !== user.id` — which **passes**, because the row is the attacker's —
50	   and then calls `mcSetMailboxPassword(mailbox.address, password)` (`:707`). Mailcow keys mailboxes
51	   by **address**, so this sets the password on the victim's real, live mailbox. The new password is
52	   returned to the attacker (`:721`).
53	
54	Cost of the attack: the price of the cheapest email plan. Impact: full read/send access to another
55	customer's business email, plus a denial of service (the victim is locked out). **This must be fixed
56	before any customer is onboarded** — the minimum fix is a global uniqueness check plus `@@unique` on
57	`EmailSubscription.domainName` and `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`, and requiring domain ownership or
58	completed DNS verification before any mailbox operation.
59	
60	### Top 10 gaps, in priority order
61	
62	1. **Stripe confirm/webhook race — customer charged, service never delivered.**
63	   `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21` credits the wallet on `checkout.session.completed`.
64	   `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27` then gets `credited === false` (P2002 replay guard in
65	   `lib/stripe.ts:242`) and **skips** `placeOrder` (`:32`), `applyResize` (`:54`) and
66	   `applyDiskExpand` (`:78`), falling through to a bare redirect. `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set in
67	   `.env`, so the webhook is live and this race is reachable today. The customer pays, the money
68	   lands in their wallet, the server is never provisioned / the resize never applied / the disk
69	   never grown — **silently, with no error**. Fulfilment must key off its own idempotency record,
70	   not off the wallet-credit flag.
71	
72	2. **SSL issuance is simulated on production and reports success.**

102	   `NXEON_SANDBOX` is set, which it is not in production. Nothing touches the VM.

2	# Nxeon — customer VM backups via vzdump
3	# Backs up all QEMU guests (running or stopped) with VMID in [100, 9000)
4	# to Proxmox storage "backup" using zstd compression, snapshot mode, keeping
5	# the last 3 backups per VM at the storage level. Templates (9000-9999) are

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Nxeon — PostgreSQL logical backups
3	# pg_dumps both databases (nxeon, nxeon_staging) as the postgres user to
4	# /tank/backup/db/, gzip-compressed with timestamped filenames, and prunes
5	# dumps older than RETENTION_DAYS. Idempotent / re-runnable.
6	set -euo pipefail
7	
8	BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
9	RETENTION_DAYS="${NXEON_DB_RETENTION_DAYS:-14}"
10	DATABASES=(nxeon nxeon_staging)
11	TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
12	
13	mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
14	
15	log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }
16	
17	rc=0
18	for db in "${DATABASES[@]}"; do
19	    # Skip cleanly if the database does not exist (e.g. staging removed).
20	    if ! sudo -u postgres psql -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='${db}'" | grep -q 1; then
21	        log "database '${db}' not present, skipping"
22	        continue
23	    fi
24	
25	    dest="${BACKUP_DIR}/${db}-${TS}.sql.gz"
26	    tmp="${dest}.partial"
27	    log "dumping '${db}' -> ${dest}"
28	    if sudo -u postgres pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges "$db" | gzip -c > "$tmp"; then
29	        mv "$tmp" "$dest"
30	        # Integrity check: gzip stream must decompress cleanly.
31	        if gunzip -t "$dest"; then
32	            log "OK ${dest} ($(du -h "$dest" | cut -f1))"
33	        else
34	            log "ERROR gunzip -t failed for ${dest}"
35	            rc=1
36	        fi
37	    else
38	        log "ERROR pg_dump failed for '${db}'"
39	        rm -f "$tmp"
40	        rc=1
41	    fi
42	done
43	
44	# Prune dumps older than RETENTION_DAYS.
45	log "pruning dumps older than ${RETENTION_DAYS} days in ${BACKUP_DIR}"
46	find "$BACKUP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sql.gz' -mtime "+${RETENTION_DAYS}" -print -delete || true
47	
48	log "done (exit ${rc})"
49	exit "$rc"

10	#   OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1                        # optional: also replicate VM dumps (large)
11	#

13

19

31	  log "psql restore returned non-zero; see ${LOG}"
32	fi
33	ERRS=$(grep -ci '^ERROR' "${LOG}" || true)
34	[ "${ERRS}" -eq 0 ] || { log "restore produced ${ERRS} errors:"; grep -i '^ERROR' "${LOG}" | head -5; fail "restore had errors"; }
35	
36	# Core tables must exist and hold rows — an empty "successful" restore is a failure.
37	for t in User OsTemplate Plan; do
38	  n=$(sudo -u postgres psql -tA "${SCRATCH}" -c "select count(*) from \"${t}\";" 2>/dev/null || echo "x")
39	  [[ "${n}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "table ${t} missing from restored dump"
40	  [ "${n}" -gt 0 ] || fail "table ${t} restored with 0 rows"
41	  log "OK ${t}=${n}"
